_agreement_is_untested_here_and_that_is_: There is NO python.py in this entry, and its absence is deliberate rather than pending.
The standard Python stack has no frequentist GLMM equivalent to lme4::glmer. The candidates
statsmodels BinomialBayesMixedGLM - variational Bayes, a different estimator targeting a
different thing; agreement with glmer would be meaningless either way.
statsmodels GEE - a POPULATION-AVERAGE model. On this fixture it targets an attenuated
quantity, not the same number by another route. Substituting it would silently swap the
estimand and the agreement check would then be comparing two different parameters and
pymer4 - wraps lme4 through rpy2, so it IS R. Two calls to the same engine agreeing is not
So this entry makes the RECOVERY claim only. harness/check.py refuses to state the agreement
claim with fewer than two engines, which is exactly the behaviour wanted: the weaker guarantee
is reported as weaker rather than dressed up.
_why_not_self_generated: The outcome is drawn from logit(p) = b0 + b1*exposed + u_j with u_j normal, which IS the random-intercept model glmer fits, so b1 is the cluster-conditional log odds ratio by construction.

recovery._calibration: NO LONGER PROVISIONAL. Measured over 300 alternative seeds of the generator, fitted with a stdlib random-intercept logistic MLE by 30-node Gauss-Hermite quadrature -- not lme4, not statsmodels -- which reproduces glmer's answer on the committed fixture to five decimals (0.360097 against 0.3601152, cluster_sd 0.645055 against 0.6450577). Conditional log OR miss: median 0.1927, 95th percentile 0.5598, maximum 0.8859. Between-cluster SD miss: median 0.0832, 95th 0.2414, maximum 0.4033. The committed seed misses by 0.3330 and 0.1549.
recovery._the_provisional_0.45_was_too_tight_and_: 0.45 was chosen so the tolerance would stay narrower than the gap between the conditional log OR (0.6931) and the crude marginal one (0.3213), on the reasoning that a wider tolerance stops distinguishing the two estimands. The calibration shows those two requirements CANNOT BOTH BE MET at 40 clusters: the sampling distribution needs 0.89 and the estimand gap allows 0.37, so roughly one run in ten of a CORRECT implementation would have failed. Narrowing a tolerance below the sampling distribution does not sharpen a check, it makes it fire on correct work.
recovery._so_the_estimand_distinction_is_carried_: A population-average model does not produce a between-cluster SD at all -- there is no such parameter in it -- so recovering 0.8 within 0.45 is a claim only a conditional model can make. That separates the two estimands STRUCTURALLY rather than by a numerical margin that the data cannot support. It is also why this entry needs per-key tolerances: 0.90 applied to a parameter whose whole miss distribution tops out at 0.40 would pass whatever it was handed.
